CHALLENGE C0016 | The claimed defect is not behaviorally material as stated. Premises: current `kappa_rate(r)` computes `rate_r = λ_r`, `peak = max(λ_0..λ_r)`, then returns `clamp(1 - λ_r / (peak + ε), 0, 1)`. If the current round is not the peak (`λ_r <= max(λ_0..λ_{r-1})`), including `λ_r` in `peak` has no effect. If the current round is the peak (`λ_r > max prior`), the intended convergence value is non-converged; the current implementation returns approximately `ε / (λ_r + ε)`, which is effectively 0 for normal positive rates and below any realistic `tau_kappa`. Concrete example: prior rates `[5, 2]`, current `1` gives `1 - 1/5 = 0.8` either way. Prior rates `[1, 2]`, current `5` gives current implementation `1 - 5/(5+ε) ≈ 0`, while excluding current and clamping gives `clamp(1 - 5/2, 0, 1) = 0`. Therefore C0016 does not establish a HIGH/CRITICAL silently-wrong result under the PoC review threshold. No SEARCH/REPLACE fix should be emitted for an unconfirmed non-material finding.

CHALLENGE C0003 | The visible code implements class-level novelty consistently with the documented equivalence-class semantics. Premises: `_novel_classes()` returns a current equivalence class as novel only if none of its members match prior findings. In an equivalence-class model, one member matching prior evidence means the class represents an already-known root cause. Concrete trace: prior round has finding `A`; current round has two same-class reports `A'` and `A''`; if `sim(A', A) >= tau`, the class is old, not novel. Returning the whole class as novel because `A''` is not individually matched would double-count rediscovery. A valid challenge would need an example where the current clustering incorrectly combines distinct root causes; that is covered by flaw-class/similarity-boundary issues such as C0015/C0008, not by the “all members must be unmatched” predicate itself.

MERGE C0007 <- C0011 | Same root cause: both findings identify over-suppression in `kappa_set()` caused by building `prior_findings` from every member of prior equivalence classes instead of a canonical/deduplicated prior representative set.

EXTEND C0015 | Additional consequence: flaw-class-blind comparison is not limited to `_compute_equivalence_classes()`. `_novel_classes()` and `_suppression_weight()` also call `self.similarity_fn(...) >= self._tau_sim()` without requiring equal `flaw_class`, so a high-similarity prior finding in a different flaw class can both mark a new class as non-novel and suppress its severity contribution. This independently supports C0015 beyond the settled `_compute_equivalence_classes()` instance in C0008.
